evidence.description: An elapsed time is divided by statistics.timePerTree and the resulting arithmetic expression is passed directly to the Int initializer without validity or range checks.

candidates.explanation: The elapsed-time calculation is converted directly to Int without validating the divisor or the resulting value. If timePerTree is zero, the division can produce infinity or NaN; a sufficiently large result can also exceed Int's range. Swift's floating-point-to-integer initializer traps for these values, so this public method has an unchecked crash path.
candidates.title: Unchecked floating-point-to-integer conversion
